lesson.title: React useEffect() hook introduction
lesson.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

steps.title: Set up counter component
steps.instructions: Create a Vite React project (npm create vite@latest, React template) and in src/MyComponent.jsx import useState and useEffect, add a count state starting at 0, a paragraph showing Count: {count}, and an Add button calling addCount (setCount(c => c + 1)). Render MyComponent from App.jsx and run npm run dev.

explanations.topic: useEffect must be imported from React alongside useState
Updater function: take previous state and add one

hints: Import both hooks in one line: import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react'.
Declare state with array destructuring: const [count, setCount] = useState(0).

Render

Count: {count}

and a
Inside addCount call setCount(c => c + 1) so it uses the previous state.
common_mistakes: Writing onClick={addCount()}, which calls the function during render instead of on click.
Forgetting to import useEffect (it's needed in the next steps).
Not rendering the component in App.jsx, so nothing appears in the browser.
Returning two sibling elements without a fragment <>...</> wrapper.

steps.title: Update title on every render
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx call useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}` }) with no dependency array so it runs on every re-render. Try adding [] to see it run only on mount, then revert.

targets.caption: Call useEffect near the top of the component
Update the document title inside the effect

explanations.topic: useEffect runs side code every time the component re-renders
useEffect takes a function and an optional dependency array
Without a dependency array the effect runs on mount and every re-render
An empty dependency array runs the effect only once on mount
When a one-time effect is appropriate (static title)

hints: Import useEffect from 'react' alongside useState, then call it near the top of your component.
Pass useEffect an arrow function as its first argument; leave out the second argument for now.
Inside the arrow function, assign a template string to document.title that inserts your count state.
Code: useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; }); then press Add and watch the browser tab title change. Try adding [] as a second argument, then remove it.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import useEffect from 'react'.
Using normal quotes instead of backticks, so ${count} appears literally in the title.
Leaving the empty [] dependency array in place, so the title only updates once on mount.
Calling useEffect inside a function, loop, or condition instead of at the top level of the component.
Writing document.Title or document.title() instead of assigning to document.title.

steps.title: Depend on count, add subtract
steps.instructions: Pass [count] as the effect's dependency array in src/MyComponent.jsx. Add a Subtract button calling subtractCount, which does setCount(c => c - 1).

targets.caption: Effect runs on mount and when count changes
The new Subtract button next to Add

explanations.topic: Adding a value to the dependency array: run on mount plus whenever that value changes
No dependency array runs the effect on every re-render, even for unrelated reasons
The title updates whether count goes up or down, because the effect depends on count

hints: The second argument to useEffect is an array. Put the state variable your effect reads inside it.
Write it as useEffect(() => { ... }, [count]);
Copy your addCount function, rename it subtractCount, and change + 1 to - 1 using the updater form: setCount(c => c - 1).
Add <button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button> and click it. The tab title should go down.
common_mistakes: Leaving the array empty ([]), so the title only updates once on mount.
Writing onClick={subtractCount()}, which calls the function during render and causes an infinite re-render loop.
Writing setCount(count - 1) instead of the updater form setCount(c => c - 1).
Forgetting to rename the copied function, which leaves two functions named addCount.

steps.title: Add color state dependency
steps.instructions: Add a color state (initial "green") with a Change color button whose changeColor toggles green/red, style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}}, and include color in the title. Make the dependency array [count, color].

targets.caption: New color state variable, starting at green
Effect re-runs when count or color changes

explanations.topic: Using the previous state with a ternary to toggle green/red
style attribute needs a JavaScript object, hence double curly braces
Without color in the dependency array, the title ignores color changes
Dependency array: effect runs whenever any listed value changes

hints: Create a second state variable with useState, initial value "green", and a button that calls a changeColor function.
In changeColor, call setColor with an updater: c => c === "green" ? "red" : "green".
Style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}} and add ${color} to document.title.
Finally change the effect's dependency array from [count] to [count, color] so the title updates on color changes.
common_mistakes: Using single braces style={color: color} instead of a double-brace object style={{color: color}}.
Forgetting to add color to the dependency array, so the title doesn't update when the color changes.
Writing onClick={changeColor()} which calls the function during render instead of passing it.
Comparing with = instead of === inside the ternary, or misspelling "green" so it never toggles back.

steps.title: Track window size with listener
steps.instructions: Rewrite src/MyComponent.jsx with width and height state from window.innerWidth/innerHeight shown in px, and a handleResize that updates both. In useEffect with [], call window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize) and console.log("EVENT LISTENER ADDED").

targets.caption: Handler updates width and height state

explanations.topic: Without useEffect, every re-render adds another resize listener
Empty dependency array: run the effect only on mount
Strict Mode runs effects twice in development (setup + cleanup cycle)

hints: You need two state variables, initialized from window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight.
Write handleResize to call setWidth(window.innerWidth) and setHeight(window.innerHeight).
Put window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize) inside useEffect(() => { ... }, []) so it only runs on mount.
Check the browser console: "EVENT LISTENER ADDED" should appear once (or twice under Strict Mode), not on every resize.
common_mistakes: Calling addEventListener directly in the component body, which adds a new listener on every render.
Omitting the empty [] dependency array, so the effect re-runs after each render.
Passing handleResize() (calling it) instead of handleResize as the callback.
Writing sethHeight / setheight with the wrong capitalization.
Forgetting to import useEffect alongside useState.

steps.title: Return a cleanup function
steps.instructions: Return a function from the effect that calls window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize) and logs "EVENT LISTENER REMOVED", then check the browser console.

targets.caption: In strict mode cleanup runs once after first mount

explanations.topic: Returning a function from useEffect for cleanup
Cleanup runs before the next re-render or on unmount
Why remove event listeners: avoid unexpected behavior and free resources
Strict mode runs the effect, cleans up, then runs it again

hints: Inside the useEffect callback, after adding the listener, return an arrow function.
In that returned function call window.removeEventListener with the same event name and handler you added.
Add console.log("EVENT LISTENER REMOVED") inside the cleanup, refresh, and open Inspect > Console.
Full shape: return () => { window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER REMOVED"); }
common_mistakes: Calling removeEventListener directly in the effect body instead of inside the returned function.
Passing a new inline function to removeEventListener instead of the same handleResize reference, so nothing is removed.
Misspelling the event name (e.g. "resized") so it doesn't match the added listener.
Writing return removeEventListener(...) which calls it immediately instead of returning a function.
Expecting the removal log only on unmount and being confused when strict mode logs it once on load.

steps.title: Add second useEffect for title
steps.instructions: Add another useEffect that sets document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}` with dependency array [width, height], then resize the window to see the title update.

targets.caption: Runs only when width or height changes
Second useEffect writes size into tab title

explanations.topic: A component can have more than one useEffect hook
Dependency array: re-run the effect when width or height updates
The effect runs on mount, then again on every size change

hints: Write a separate useEffect below the one that adds the resize listener. Don't edit the existing one.
Inside the effect, assign a template string to document.title using the width and height state variables.
Pass [width, height] as the second argument so the effect re-runs when either value changes.
useEffect(() => { document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}`; }, [width, height]);
common_mistakes: Using quotes instead of backticks, so ${width} appears literally in the title.
Leaving out the dependency array, which makes the effect run on every render, or using [], which makes the title never update after mount.
Putting the title code inside the resize-listener effect that has an empty dependency array, so the title only updates once.
Looking for the size on the page instead of in the browser tab title.
